title: Per-route usage attribution and hybrid pricing model requirements
text:
Per-route usage attribution and hybrid pricing model requirements

description:
Background: As Redwood expands product differentiation (hosted API + dedicated + private), customers are requesting more granular billing: different unit economics per API route (e.g., /generate vs /chat vs /embed), per-model overrides, and mixed-model subscriptions (a base plan + add-on bundles). Current billing aggregates token and embedding units into a single usage stream which makes per-route attribution, quota enforcement, and invoice-level visibility inaccurate for these customers.

Goal: Define PRD-level requirements and acceptance criteria for implementing per-route usage attribution, hybrid pricing (base plan + route-level add-ons), and consistent overage handling so that invoices and customer-facing consoles match internal meters and financial reconciliation.

Scope (in):
- Metering and persistent attribution of every request to a route id, product SKU, and pricing tier.
- Quotas that can be configured at multiple scopes: api-key, organization, project, and plan-level pooled quotas.
- Price table mapping: route -> model variant -> unit cost (tokens/embeddings/requests).
- Soft overage behavior: configurable grace windows and notifications before billing.
- Invoice line-item generation that mirrors the per-route aggregation used internally.
- Audit logs and reconciliation exports for accounting and SOC review.

Scope (out):
- Changes to core tokenization heuristics or model inference pricing itself (handled by finance).
- Deep UI design for billing console (we will provide acceptance hooks and wireframes; detailed design will be separate).

Key stakeholders: Miguel (PM owner), Finance: Lina Park, Billing Eng: Rohit Iyer, Runtime Eng: Aisha Kapoor, Console UX: Jamal Reyes, Legal/Compliance: Priya Mehta, Customer Success: Nora Chen.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Cost of fine-grained attribution vs. performance: per-request attribution adds metadata writes to metering pipeline. We should use write-batch windows to reduce overhead while keeping max reconciliation delta < 0.1% by volume.
- Quota enforcement locality: enforcing at edge (low latency) vs. central (accurate). Hybrid approach proposed: local short-term counters + periodic reconciliation with central quota authority for hard blocks.
- Overage charging cadence: immediate micro-billing (complex) vs. monthly invoice-based billing (simpler). Proposal: support monthly invoice line items and an optional enterprise real-time overage webhook.

Telemetry and schema requirements:
- Every event must include: timestamp_iso, request_id, route_id, model_id, api_key_hash, org_id, project_id, token_count, embed_units, compute_unit_estimate, pricing_sku, region.
- New price table service with versioned mappings (pricing_sku -> unit_costs; route_pattern -> sku).

Acceptance criteria (see separate list) and test cases defined below.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Metering: For a mixed workload (10k generate, 5k chat, 2k embed requests) the billing export groups usage into routes and matches the runtime aggregator with a reconciliation delta <= 0.1% for token counts and embed units.
2) Attribution: Each invoice line item must include route_id, model_tag, unit_cost, units_consumed, and subtotal. Line items for add-ons must be shown separately and reconcile to the price table version active during usage window.
3) Quotas: Customers with pooled org-level quotas and per-project soft limits must be prevented from exceeding hard org quota. Enforcement should allow local short-term bursts up to configured burst_capacity and then throttle with HTTP 429 and structured error specifying remaining_quota and reset_window_seconds.
4) Overages: Soft overage window (configurable) allows up to X% beyond quota for grace_period; after grace_period, usage is billed as overage at the configured overage_rate. Finance test: run simulated overage and verify line-item overage charge on monthly invoice PDF and in billing export CSV.
5) Price table versioning: Changing a pricing mapping mid-billing-cycle must not affect prior usage. Billing export must include pricing_table_version_id to ensure immutable reconciliation. Test by flipping route price in staging and verify old usage still billed using prior version for that time range.
6) Rate limits: Per-route rate limits with tiered windows (per-second and per-minute) should be enforced and surfaced in API headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Integration test: simulate sustained traffic and assert headers reflect limits and counters decrement appropriately.
7) Telemetry completeness: Metering pipeline must surface for any sampled request the full required schema fields and reject or flag events missing critical attribution fields. End-to-end test: inject malformed events and assert they are flagged in the reconciliation report with counts and example request_ids.
8) Invoice parity: For 3 enterprise customers with different plan configurations (base + per-route add-on; metered-only; pooled enterprise), monthly invoices generated by billing job must match aggregated export and show identical totals to Finance's ledger within rounding rules. Manual Finance sign-off required as acceptance gate.
9) Console display: Billing Console mock should show per-route breakdown for the current month and allow exporting the same CSV that finance uses. UX acceptance: PM + Console lead sign-off on mock data fidelity and labels.
10) Security & audit: Audit logs for any pricing change must capture actor, timestamp, old_price, new_price, and reason. Security review required for change management flows (flagged in the ticket) and tests must show audit trail for at least 90 days in staging exports.
11) Backfill and migration: When enabling per-route attribution for existing customers, a backfill job must produce a reconciliation delta report; for first release, delta must be explained and approved by Finance before enabling billing for historical windows.
12) Performance: Added metering overhead (p50 request latency impact) must be < 8ms for 95% of requests in standard traffic profiles. Performance tests must be included in CI benchmarks.

notes:
- Prototype approach discussed in meeting 2026-03-05: create a lightweight attribution tag at the ingress that is propagated with the request context to runtime and metering pipeline.
- Rohit recommended a single append-only metering table with eventual compaction to simplify reconciliation; Runtime team prefers a sharded write pattern for throughput. Decision deferred to architecture spike (ENG-42198).
- Finance requires clear mapping between pricing SKUs and GL codes. Lina will supply SKU->GL mapping by 2026-03-18.
- Customer Success flagged two customers (Acme Health, Datawise) who need per-route reporting in the next billing cycle; treat as high-priority commercial enablement once alpha is ready.
